scenes.tts: In the Clarity A D trial, one thousand seven hundred ninety five people had mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease. Amyloid was confirmed in all of them. They were randomly given the antibody leh-KAN-eh-mab or a placebo for eighteen months. Did the treated group get better? They did not. Both groups got worse, and the question is by how much.
scenes.caption: In the Clarity AD trial, 1,795 people had mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease. Amyloid was confirmed in all of them. They were randomly given the antibody lecanemab or a placebo for eighteen months. Did the treated group get better? They did not. Both groups got worse, and the question is by how much.
scenes.visual: Two group boxes, lecanemab and placebo, each with a rating dial; question mark over the treated box; both pointers drift upward.
scenes.narration: In the Clarity AD trial, 1,795 people had mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease. Amyloid was confirmed in all of them. They were randomly given the antibody lecanemab or a placebo for eighteen months. Did the treated group get better? They did not. Both groups got worse, and the question is by how much.

scenes.tts: The outcome was a score called C D R S B, the Clinical Dementia Rating, Sum of Boxes. A clinician rates cognition and daily function. The score runs from zero to eighteen. Higher means worse, so a rise on this scale is a worsening.
scenes.caption: The outcome was a score called CDR-SB, the Clinical Dementia Rating, Sum of Boxes. A clinician rates cognition and daily function. The score runs from zero to eighteen. Higher means worse, so a rise on this scale is a worsening.
scenes.visual: A horizontal scale from 0 to 18 labelled higher means worse; a marker moves right and the word worsening appears.
scenes.narration: The outcome was a score called CDR-SB, the Clinical Dementia Rating, Sum of Boxes. A clinician rates cognition and daily function. The score runs from zero to eighteen. Higher means worse, so a rise on this scale is a worsening.

scenes.tts: Adjusted mean changes at eighteen months were plus one point two one with leh-KAN-eh-mab. With placebo they were plus one point six six. Both are rises, so the treated group did not improve. It worsened less. That gap is some of the strongest evidence that removing amyloid changes the disease, and also evidence that the drug did not stop it.
scenes.caption: Adjusted mean changes at eighteen months were +1.21 with lecanemab. With placebo they were +1.66. Both are rises, so the treated group did not improve. It worsened less. That gap is some of the strongest evidence that removing amyloid changes the disease, and also evidence that the drug did not stop it.
scenes.visual: Two bars rising from a zero line: placebo 1.66, lecanemab 1.21; both above zero; a gap marked between their tops.
scenes.narration: Adjusted mean changes at eighteen months were +1.21 with lecanemab. With placebo they were +1.66. Both are rises, so the treated group did not improve. It worsened less. That gap is some of the strongest evidence that removing amyloid changes the disease, and also evidence that the drug did not stop it.

scenes.tts: First, the absolute difference. It is a plain subtraction of two amounts of worsening. One point six six minus one point two one is zero point four five points less worsening. The paper reports a difference of minus zero point four five points. Its confidence interval runs from minus zero point six seven to minus zero point two three.
scenes.caption: First, the absolute difference. It is a plain subtraction of two amounts of worsening. 1.66 − 1.21 is 0.45 points less worsening. The paper reports a difference of −0.45 points. Its confidence interval runs from −0.67 to −0.23.
scenes.visual: The gap between the bar tops is filled and labelled 0.45 points; subtraction written beside; the paper's value and interval appear on an interval line.
scenes.narration: First, the absolute difference. It is a plain subtraction of two amounts of worsening. 1.66 − 1.21 is 0.45 points less worsening. The paper reports a difference of −0.45 points. Its confidence interval runs from −0.67 to −0.23.

scenes.tts: Second, relative slowing. Use the placebo change as the base. Think of the placebo bar as the whole decline. Zero point four five divided by one point six six is zero point two seven one. That is about twenty seven percent. Check it. One point six six times zero point seven two nine gives one point two one.
scenes.caption: Second, relative slowing. Use the placebo change as the base. Think of the placebo bar as the whole decline. 0.45 divided by 1.66 is 0.271. That is about 27%. Check it. 1.66 × 0.729 gives 1.21.
scenes.visual: The placebo bar becomes the whole; its top 0.45 slice is shaded as the share removed; fraction 0.45 over 1.66 equals 0.271, about 27%; check line.
scenes.narration: Second, relative slowing. Use the placebo change as the base. Think of the placebo bar as the whole decline. 0.45 divided by 1.66 is 0.271. That is about 27%. Check it. 1.66 × 0.729 gives 1.21.

scenes.tts: So what does twenty seven percent mean? It compares two amounts of decline. It is not a twenty seven percent gain in memory. It is not a fraction of patients helped. It is not anyone's prognosis. Relative slowing is a share of the placebo decline, and the treated group still worsened.
